* you · 1
Using the saved Atlas notebook only, explain in under 250 words why the Adobe October window does not establish Artcraft-caused revenue loss. Cite evidence IDs and propose one discriminating public observation.
* model · 2
Fact: the October record shows attention, not displacement. PhotoCraft maintainers call it early alpha, not a daily professional Photoshop replacement, and report gaps in tools, typography, workflows and plug-ins (E01). HN/press show diffusion across audiences, but are salience/reach, not production parity or paid migration (E03, E04, E05; E02). Adobe’s Q3 FY2026 predates the episode and reports revenue growth and ARR, so it cannot isolate Artcraft impact (E08). The October ADBE/QQQ window is a short descriptive n=4 buy-and-hold difference, beta=1, explicitly not causal (E09). Crucially, no verified cancellation cohort, paid-seat migration, exposed-seat revenue bridge, independent parity benchmark, borrow or options data exists (E10). Inference: without capability, adoption, economics or clean event attribution, the window cannot establish Artcraft-caused revenue loss. Assumption: professional Adobe workflows depend on file fidelity, plug-ins, collaboration and procurement; unverified.

Discriminating observation: a pre-registered, independent blind trial with paying creative professionals on original PSD/PRPROJ/LR files, measuring task completion without Adobe fallback, time-to-finish, fidelity, crashes, colour and plug-in interoperability (E01, E10). This directly opens or closes the capability gate; only if it passes do paid-adoption and revenue tests become meaningful.

* say ▸  (RET to message the task, C-Enter to steer it)
